entities.summary: Crateuas (b. 200 BCE, Kingdom of Pontus) was a scientist or inventor of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in the Kingdom of Pontus. He is known for his contributions to the field of logicians & mathematicians. Crateuas' work on geometric problems and his development of a new method for calculating the volume of a pyramid were particularly influential. His work was later adopted by scholars in the Hellenistic period, including Euclid, who built upon Crateuas' discoveries. Crateuas' legacy can be seen in the many mathematical problems and theorems that bear his name, including the 'Crateuas' theorem' and the 'Crateuas' method for calculating the volume of a pyramid. Crateuas' contributions to the field of mathematics were recognized by the Roman Emperor Augustus, who awarded him a grant of land and a noble title. Crateuas' work on mathematics was also influential in the development of astronomy, as his calculations on the movement of the planets were used by later astronomers to develop their theories. The discovery of Crateuas' tomb in the ancient city of Pontus, Greece, has provided valuable insights into the life and work of this important figure in the history of mathematics. The Crateuas' theorem has been used in various fields, including physics and engineering, and continues to be an important tool in the study of mathematical problems. Crateuas' work on mathematics has had a lasting impact on the development of Western mathematics, and his legacy continues to be celebrated by scholars and mathematicians today.
